:::{#exm-zip-reg}
#### Zero-inflated Poisson probabilities and moments

Suppose that at some covariate pattern and exposure,
a zero-inflated Poisson regression model (@def-zip-reg)
has $\pi = 0.3$ and $\mu_0 = 2$.
By the solution to @exr-zinf-pmf,

$$
\ba
\P(Y = 0 \mid \vX = \vx, T = t)
&= \pi + (1 - \pi) \expf{-\mu_0}
&& \text{(zero-inflated PMF at 0)} \\
&= 0.3 + 0.7 \expf{-2}
&& \text{(substitute)} \\
&\approx 0.3 + 0.7 \cdot 0.135
&& \text{(} \expf{-2} \approx 0.135 \text{)} \\
&\approx 0.395
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\ea
$$

and by the solution to @exr-zinf-moments,

$$
\ba
\E{Y \mid \vX = \vx, T = t}
&= (1 - \pi) \mu_0
&& \text{(zero-inflated mean)} \\
&= 0.7 \cdot 2
&& \text{(substitute)} \\
&= 1.4
&& \text{(multiply)} \\
\Var{Y \mid \vX = \vx, T = t}
&= (1 - \pi) \mu_0 (1 + \pi \mu_0)
&& \text{(zero-inflated variance)} \\
&= 1.4 \cdot (1 + 0.3 \cdot 2)
&& \text{(substitute)} \\
&= 1.4 \cdot 1.6
&& \text{(multiply and add)} \\
&= 2.24
&& \text{(multiply)}
\ea
$$

A Poisson distribution with the same mean, $1.4$,
has variance $1.4$
and $\P(Y = 0) = \expf{-1.4} \approx 0.247$.
The zero-inflated model has both more zeros
($0.395$ versus $0.247$)
and a larger variance
($2.24$ versus $1.4$),
so it is [overdispersed](#def-overdispersion) relative to that Poisson model.

:::
